title: Korea Delivery Fee Fairness Board
oneLiner: A Korean small-restaurant scorecard that compares delivery app commissions, ad pressure, hidden terms, and direct-order escape paths.
previewUrl: pending Stitch export in Phase B
targetUser: Korean restaurant owners deciding whether Baemin/Coupang Eats/Yogiyo-style channels are sustainable after commission, ad, and promotion pressure.
keyUx: Enter app terms, order volume, ad spend, discounts, and direct-order capacity; the app scores fairness and drafts a customer-facing direct-order nudge.
spread_trigger: Owners share the fairness score with staff or peers to justify steering customers direct.
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app called "Korea Delivery Fee Fairness Board" for Korean restaurant owners deciding whether Baemin/Coupang Eats/Yogiyo-style channels are sustainable after commission, ad, and promotion pressure.. The app is based on observed user pull from S8: Family-run restaurant operators describe online ordering and delivery as one-sided and profit-killing. S9: A Korean government survey found delivery apps take an average 8.2 percent cut, nearly double what restaurant owners say they can sustain. The app should use a Fee Fairness Board around the trigger moment "Enter app terms, order volume, ad spend, discounts, and direct-order capacity; the app scores fairness and drafts a customer-facing direct-order nudge." and make the first screen communicate "A Korean small-restaurant scorecard that compares delivery app commissions, ad pressure, hidden terms, and direct-order escape paths.". Build the core workflow around user-entered evidence and produce delivery platform fairness receipt. Required sections: Platform term comparison; Commission sustainability meter; Ad pressure ledger; Promo loss calculator; Direct-order readiness checklist; Customer nudge copy; Owner fairness score receipt. Emotional pressure to make visible: 자산 방어. Design direction: use the financial-analyst profile with rigorous margin workbench with compact Korean-market fee tables, quiet variance chips, and decision-oriented owner notes. Avoid generic dashboard framing; make the main interaction feel like Fee Fairness Board.

sourceSignals.source: Reddit r/restaurant, 2026, small restaurant owners handling online ordering and delivery fees
sourceSignals.evidence: Family-run restaurant operators describe online ordering and delivery as one-sided and profit-killing.
sourceSignals.action: Owners seek advice on alternatives, direct ordering, minimums, and how to avoid app dependency.

sourceSignals.source: Korea Herald, 2026, Korean restaurants trapped by delivery apps
sourceSignals.evidence: A Korean government survey found delivery apps take an average 8.2 percent cut, nearly double what restaurant owners say they can sustain.
sourceSignals.action: Restaurant owners need a way to compare app terms, advertising pressure, and sustainable commission levels.
